fact_english: Apolinario Mabini, paralysed in the legs, was carried to Kawit in a hammock by relays of bearers (when exactly he arrived is weak in the sources, so it is not said). In his memoir La Revolución Filipina he judged the 12 June 1898 proclamation premature and imprudent (the trivia gives the gist, not a quotation). The Acta proclaims independence under the protection of the North American nation; in Paris, six months later (Treaty of Paris, 10 December 1898), Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States. Rajah Sulayman was a real ruler of Maynila who fought the Spaniards in 1570 to 1571; his voice in the medallion is the story's invention. Sources as named in story/ep08_v2/facts.md: Mabini's memoir, the Acta, Ambeth Ocampo, Wikipedia (Apolinario Mabini; Rajah Sulayman). facts.md names no source for the Paris cession (it points to Episode 5's facts): the best it gives is the Acta/Wikipedia row; check Episode 5's sources before posting.

lines.speaker: INDIO
lines.text: Tiyak: dumating si Mabini sa Kawit na buhat sa duyan.
lines.say: Tiyak: dumating si maBIni sa KAwit na buhat sa duyan.

lines.speaker: INDIO
lines.text: Sa alaala niya, isinulat niyang maaga pa at padalos-dalos ang pagpapahayag: diwa ito, hindi sipi.

lines.speaker: INDIO
lines.text: Totoong pinuno siya ng Maynila na lumaban sa mga Espanyol noong 1570.
lines.say: Totoong pinuno siya ng Maynila na lumaban sa mga Espanyol noong mil kinyentos setenta.

lines.speaker: INDIO
lines.text: Ang tinig niya sa medalyon, kuwento namin.

after_text: Ikaw, ka-Indio: kung isang hakbang na lang pauwi, at may nagsabing "huwag muna", makikinig ka ba?
